newsitem.title: USA: Alex. Brown sees no more cutbacks ahead of merger.
newsitem.headline: Alex. Brown sees no more cutbacks ahead of merger.

text.p: Alex Brown Inc, the retail broker merging with Bankers Trust, said Monday it did not expect any more cutbacks beyond the ones that will stem from its exiting fixed-rate municipal finance.
"This is basically the only shoe to drop," said Mayo Shattuck, president of the Baltimore-based brokerage, in a telephone interview with Reuters.

"The most significant (decision) is that we are exiting the municipal origination business." Shattuck said the firm opted to stay in the variable rate part of the municipal business as Bankers Trust is active in that arena. "They do not operate at the long end of the curve, nor now do we."
And Alex Brown, which wants to finish its merger with Bankers Trust by year-end, will stay in the business of converting debt to equity, an area it considers key.

The firm, established in 1800, primarily was picked by Bankers for its strength in underwriting equities. Considered a crown jewel by some security analysts, Alex Brown underwrote $188 million worth of Initial Public Offerings as of May 2, putting it in 12th place, according to Newark-New Jersey based Securities Data Co.

While the brokerage underwrote about half as many municipal bonds, $99.1 million, that only put it in 59th place, due to the vast difference in the size of the two markets. Only $7 billion IPOs have been sold so far this year, a fraction of the $55 billion of new municipal issues that have hit the market, Securities Data said.

Razor-thin spreads on municipal offerings have forced a number of players to bow out of underwriting in recent years, and Alex. Brown made it clear that its decision to exit the fixed-rate public finance area, a step that affects 160 of its 2,700 employees, was not driven by the merger. "In all likelihood, we would have done it in the absence of the merger," Shattuck said.
